az_obscenity_wall.blurb: A small trad wall in the Sycamore Canyon basalt cliffs of Paradise Forks, in a pine forest roughly half an hour west of Flagstaff. It holds five routes: two at 5.8 and three around 5.11, so it suits climbers who want a couple of moderate lines alongside some harder finger-crack work. The basalt is solid in the upper part of the wall but poor lower down, which means many lines begin from ledges partway up the cliff. Across the Forks as a whole, crack climbing dominates, protection tends to be excellent, and most climbs are short, topping out near 90 feet.

az_fin_the_2.blurb: A tall face of red stone rising above Dry Creek Road in west Sedona, just north of the Devil's Bridge site. Five trad routes of two to four pitches each go up it, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.10 range with a single route at the hard end of the 5.13 grades. The wall is a place for multi-pitch climbing rather than quick laps. The walk in is easy if you aim for the left end of the formation and follow the trail, and you should not try to charge straight at the base from the road.

az_lookout_tower.blurb: A spire of about 120 feet on the east side of Fay Canyon, west of Sedona, with views over the surrounding red rock country. Five trad routes climb it, one at 5.8, three at 5.10 and one at 5.11-, with a two-pitch 5.10 line as the standout. The rock bands here are unusual even by Sedona standards. From the Fay Canyon trailhead, follow the canyon trail for several minutes, then branch off on a climbers' path that threads up through the cliff bands; the foot of the south side is roughly half an hour from the car.

az_oak_creek_spire.blurb: A double-summited tower at the east end of Jacks Canyon Road near the Village of Oak Creek, south of Sedona. Its five trad routes run three to six pitches and span roughly 5.9 to 5.12, with climbs on both the north and south faces, so it is a day for experienced trad climbers rather than beginners. The tower is noted for carrying more loose rock than other Sedona spires, so a helmet and extra care are advised. A well-known move partway up requires leaping across the gap between the two summits. The approach is cross-country and drops into a wash.

az_upper_religion_wall.blurb: A trad wall of five routes in the Church Spires area near the Chapel of the Holy Cross, sitting directly above the Lower Religion Wall. Grades start around 5.8 and reach 5.12, with a spread through the 5.9 and 5.10 range, so there is something for both moderate and strong leaders. The walk from the road takes about 30 to 45 minutes and finishes with a short fourth-class scramble at the top of a wash. Reaching the wall means first climbing one of the Lower Religion Wall's routes.
az_upper_religion_wall.parking_note: Take Chapel Road east from Highway 179 and leave the car in the pullout on the north side, before the gate and the chapel's own lot.
az_upper_religion_wall.approach: Walk through the chapel lot to the climbers' trail at its east edge, follow it about a quarter mile to a mountain bike trail, then continue a short way to the big roof. Go up the wash on the left, scramble a short fourth-class section at its top, and take the trail to the cliff base.

az_lower_beach.blurb: A small crag of five routes within the Beach Areas of Twin Butte, near Sedona, set directly above the Planetarium and catching sun into the afternoon. Three of the routes are trad and two are sport, with grades running from the high 5.8s to the 5.11s, concentrated around 5.10. It works as a short outing for climbers who want a mix of gear and bolted lines. The approach uses the trail past the Planetarium turn-off, then turns up a steep drainage to the cliffs. A neighbouring wall higher up is reached by walking along the base from here.

az_teapot_the.blurb: A formation on Mitten Ridge, north of Schnebly Hill Road near Sedona, also known as Teapot Rock. Five routes, mostly trad with one sport line, run from 5.9 to 5.11, and the headline climb is a five-pitch outing. The traverse across it is sunny and exposed, while lines up the spout can be sunny or shady depending on which one you pick. Park at the first large pullout on the left off the road, follow the trail up the wash, then take a climbers' trail north and uphill to start at the west end.
